chapter: Banjo, piano and his own bands
title: Recording session with Kid Thomas and George's borrowed banjo
summary: Asked about a recording session with Kid Thomas and George, he recalls little but tells how George borrowed his banjos and never returned one.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you more about that recording session with Kid Thomas.
You know when you went over there with George? You went with George? Yeah.
I went with George, but I forgot. I know George was playing and Kid Thomas was playing, but I don't know where the rest of him was.
Well, you went. I went with him, yeah. Yeah. And he had my banjo. He didn't know about my banjo. And he never did have one.

He was nothing. My annoyance. Every time he wanted one, he'd come to me. He said, Man, let me get your banjo. I said, Okay, George. When I had two, three of them banjos, I just got rid of one. I sold.
I always had two banjos. You know what I mean? I've been having that for about four years. But what kind of... Well, you say he borrowed one once and went to Jackson, huh?
Went to Jackson, yeah. And never did give it back to him. Never did.
Well, did he hock them or what? I don't know what he'd done to him. No, he didn't hock them.
